subject: Budget signal debrief — pilot gating & batching asks
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit@novumtech.com>; Tanya Ramaswamy <tanya@novumtech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 Apr 2027 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Budget signal debrief — pilot gating & batching asks

Hi Amit / Tanya,

Thanks again for taking time today — appreciate the candid budget context. Quick recap from our side and three concrete asks so we can lock the pilot gate.

1) Key pain & goals we heard
- High volume of short text classifications (~35M requests/month) with unpredictable peak windows.
- Target: reduce per-classification cost by ~60% while keeping >=98% precision on priority labels.
- Goal timeline: initial pilot in Q3 (proof-of-value in 6 weeks).

2) Economics framing we proposed
- Token economics: 1) move batching at gateway to reduce model tokens by 40–55% for typical streams; 2) prefix/KV caching for repeat contexts (expected 10–20% additional savings).
- Modeled ROI: assuming 35M req/mo and 1.8 avg tokens per request, our attached spreadsheet shows a 48–62% unit-cost reduction under conservative latency constraints.

3) Three asks to qualify pilot gate (what we need from NovumTech)
- Budget signal: a confirmed Q3 pilot commit range (example: $100k–$180k) so we size dedicated pool + burst.
- Test data slice: 100k representative records (anonymized) and a brief sequence-length distribution CSV.
- Ops SLA clarity: acceptable tail latency (p50/p95/p99) and any hard SLAs for peak windows.

Attachments: novum-batching-savings-model.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB) — conservative and optimistic tabs; MAP-v1.pdf (one-page mutual action plan).

Next steps I suggest:
- You share budget signal and the test data slice by Wed 5/3.
- We run a 2-week validation on hosted with a dedicated burst plan and share a short readout.

If that aligns, I’ll draft a simple SOW + pilot runbook and loop in our solutions engineer (Jasmine).

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Budget signal debrief — pilot gating & batching asks

Priyom — thanks for the clear recap. Quick responses inline: 

- Budget: we can likely swing a Q3 pilot in the $140k–$160k band. That’s a conditional signal: procurement will want a 6‑week POC readout before broader commit.
- Data: we can deliver a 100k anonymized sample by Mon 5/3. I’ll have engineering drop the CSV with sequence lengths and a distribution.
- Latency: target p95 < 250ms, p99 < 600ms for the classification path. During our morning spikes (7–9AM PT) we can tolerate up to 800ms p99 for 10 minutes if we have staged fallback.

Couple of asks for you: can you include in the SOW the fallback policy (model variant + regional failover) and a clear cost estimate for burst vs reserved capacity? We need to show procurement the upper bound.

Appreciate the attachments — I’ll take a look and get back with comments.

—Amit
Head of ML Engineering, NovumTech
amit@novumtech.com

Priyom — quick internal note to capture Ops/SE next steps before I draft the SOW: 

1) Sizing: use conservative case from the spreadsheet (35M req/mo, 1.8 tokens/req, 40% batching reduction) to size reserved pool. Show a burst+reserved cost ladder with 0%, 25%, 50% burst usage.
2) Fallback policy: propose model-variant (quantized 4-bit) in eu-west for failover + region routing rules. Include estimated latency delta in the doc.
3) Measurement: define success metric for pilot as 'per-classification cost reduction' and 'precision retention (delta <=1.5%)'.
4) Deliverables & timing: SOW draft EOW (5/6), test-data ingest/runbook by 5/10, 2-week validation run 5/17–5/31, readout 6/3.

Priyom — I’ll start the SOW with those bullets; Jasmine, can you slot SE coverage for 5/17 validation and confirm if we need any presigned S3 links for data?
